hook: The $25 chopper and the $25 slicer solve different problems.

scenes.visual_prompt: Two product boxes side by side on a counter, both with a '$24.97' price sticker overlay — the Fullstar chopper and the Mueller Pro mandoline.
scenes.voiceover: These two tools are both $24.97. They are not the same tool.

scenes.visual_prompt: Split screen: left shows diced onion dropping from the chopper, right shows thin even potato rounds falling from the mandoline.
scenes.voiceover: One dices for stuffing and gravy. The other slices thin, even rounds for a gratin.

scenes.visual_prompt: A sweet potato gratin being layered in a baking dish using the uniform mandoline-cut rounds, close-up of the even layering.
scenes.voiceover: If your menu has a layered side — sweet potato gratin, scalloped potatoes — the mandoline earns its spot.

scenes.visual_prompt: Extreme close-up of the mandoline blade glinting under light, with the plastic finger guard sitting unused on the counter beside it.
scenes.voiceover: Reviewers warn this blade cuts a fingertip as easily as a potato — skip the guard and regret it.

scenes.visual_prompt: Hand correctly using the finger guard over the mandoline, clean uniform potato slices falling steadily below.
scenes.voiceover: During a week the kitchen moves faster than usual, that guard is the line between prep and urgent care.

scenes.visual_prompt: Simple decision-tree graphic: 'Mostly dicing? Skip it.' on one side, 'Layered dish? Buy it.' on the other, blog icon at bottom.
scenes.on_screen_text: Which one does your menu need?
scenes.voiceover: I broke down both tools against five Thanksgiving prep tasks — link in bio.

caption: Two $24.97 tools, two completely different jobs. One dices your stuffing base, the other slices gratin-thin rounds — and only one of them needs a safety lecture. I compared both against what Thanksgiving prep actually requires. Full writeup on the blog (link in bio).
